synopsis: Komatsu’s KomVision Human Detection and Collision Mitigation system went on sale on the PC200-11 excavator in Japan in December 2019, was announced on 30 March 2020, and was followed by the PC200i-12 in December 2024 [f1640, f10633]. The research found no dedicated Japanese off-road automatic-braking rule or identified coverage and testing requirements, but unverified rules leave regulatory status uncertain rather than proving absence [f2308, f15593, f2813, f2871]. General construction-machinery safety provisions apply, but neither an automatic-braking mandate nor the absence of relevant AI legislation should be inferred from the research gaps [f2309, f2394]. A Japanese simulator study published in 2020 found that drivers trusting other vehicles’ AEB braked later; this suggests a possible parallel for ground crew around automatically braking machines, but remains on-road comparison evidence, not evidence about mining operators [f3423, f3462, f3463, f3457]. NIED and JARI in Japan are named alongside French and German facilities as principal ground-truth sources for weather models [f16122].
